requirement_text.REQ-048: Port src/engine/instance.zig's InstanceStore.completeTask() (per src/design/engine.md "Section EE-04: Complete Task", L1632) as complete_task/N, operating on REQ-043's tasks table and REQ-044's transition/3. Accepts a task_id and an output_variables map. output_variables may be an empty map (valid, EE-04 AC5); nil is rejected with a distinct error (EE-04 edge case: "use {} for no output"). A task_id that does not exist returns a distinct not-found error (EE-04 AC2). A task whose status is not PENDING (already COMPLETED or CANCELLED) returns a distinct conflict error (EE-04 AC3) -- these two are separately pattern-matchable, not one generic error. In ONE transaction (EE-04 AC4): merge output variables per REQ-049's EE-09 merge, evaluate outgoing edge conditions via REQ-044/REQ-050, activate the next node(s) via REQ-047's activation path, flip the task to COMPLETED with completed_by/completed_at/output_variables set, and append a TASK_COMPLETED event via REQ-025. Row-level locking (SELECT ... FOR UPDATE on the task or the instance) serialises two concurrent completions of the same task so exactly one wins -- this is the EE-12 concurrency property, exercised concretely here and stated generally in REQ-055. SCOPE BOUNDARY: POST /api/v1/tasks/:id/complete is S4 (api-surface). R-Co's EE-04 AC bullets are written as HTTP status codes (404/409/422); this requirement returns the corresponding tagged tuples and the S4 layer owns the status mapping, exactly as REQ-025's is_duplicate boolean left the 200-vs-201 choice to S4. Likewise EE-04's edge case "TASK_WORKER completing a task assigned to a different user: HTTP 403 (per IDN-03 role matrix)" is an authorization concern belonging to the S4 auth plug (REQ-021's precedent) -- name it explicitly as out of scope here rather than partially implementing a role check inside the engine.
